source.title: General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System, Childs collection
source.inspection: The complete source page and enlarged message crops were visually inspected. Literal invalid source glyphs are retained; no editorial plaintext repair changes this transcription.

editorial_notes: The same-length candidate changes BUD9PEST to BUDAPEST and FUPKSPRUCH to FUNKSPRUCH; the certificate records the precise source-coordinate cost.
The reader-facing spelling unterliegt adds an E to raw UNTERLIGT. That extra plaintext character is an editorial orthographic restoration, not part of the fixed-length re-encryption certificate.
Raw CENSUR is retained as historical spelling; punctuation and word spacing are editorial.

editorial_notes: The printed C in group ACVGD is outside the ADFGVX coordinate alphabet. It remains C in the literal source and is masked as one coordinate erasure only for analysis.
KOPENHAGEN is the likely place-name; it repairs the raw KOPENH?HEN. The certificate distinguishes the invalid-glyph fill from changes to valid printed coordinates.
Filittis, Rheinbaben and Horstmann are retained as decoded names without identifying the individuals.

editorial_notes: All 154 raw plaintext characters are fixed by valid source coordinates and the complete published key; no source correction is used.
The reader-facing Mel[d]ungen supplies the missing D in raw MELUNGEN. This is an editorial spelling restoration, not a new decrypted character or a coordinate repair.
B.M.K. and NATEKO are retained without an unsupported expansion. ROEM 2 is a literal reference to a Roman numeral, presented without changing the raw digit.
The page heading and internal stamp are 3 November, while the reception header prints 5 November. Both are retained.
